chunks: Those who avoid the greater sins and shameful acts, except minor trespasses, your Lord's forgiveness surely has great amplitude. He is fully knowledgeable of you as He produced you from the earth, and since you were a foetus in your mother's womb. So do not assert your goodness; he is better who takes heed and preserves himself.

key_terms.فَلَا تُزَكُّوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ: so do not assert your goodness

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about avoiding major sins and minor slips?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the term 'al-Lamam' (minor slips) is often interpreted as the inevitable minor sins that do not constitute persistent major transgression, highlighting a balance between striving for perfection and acknowledging human frailty. This verse serves as a foundational argument against the claim of absolute self-purity (Tazkiyah al-Nafs), emphasizing that true Taqwa (God-consciousness) is known only to Allah, who created humans from dust and the womb. It underscores the divine attribute of 'Wasi' al-Maghfirah' (Vast Forgiveness) for those who consistently avoid major sins, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on continuous self-reflection rather than self-deification.
